why: Collapses wallBlocksPath's horizon loop to a single iteration REGARDLESS of the `ticks` argument any caller passes -- the actual pre-#224 defect (the probe establishes only that the very next step is legal), and a stricter target than mutating the AI_PATH_HORIZON_TICKS constant, which a caller passing an explicit tick count (targeting.test.ts's speed-scaling case) would launder. Measured at 4 of 107 scoped tests failing: targeting.test.ts's 'rejects a heading that is clear for one tick but walled a few ticks later' (the tick-8 hull position is never probed once i is capped at 1) and 'scales its reach with the speed it is handed, not with a hardcoded one' (its wall sits at the tick-10 position, unreachable once the loop stops after tick 1, regardless of speed), plus danger.test.ts's 'rejects a preferred side that is clear for one tick but walled within the horizon' and 'refuses a sidestep candidate that steps toward an armed mine' (both call wallBlocksPath directly in their own assertions, so the collapse also corrupts what those tests use to check the production result).
